state.misconception_label: Confuses the order of operations, believes addition comes before multiplication

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: \[ 3 \times 2+4-5 \] Where do the brackets need to go to make the answer equal \( 13 \) ? I got Does not need brackets because I worked left to right instead of following the order of operations.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Think of it like making a sandwich. First, you put the bread down (multiplication), then you add the toppings (addition), and finally, you take away any ingredients you don't want (subtraction). If you mix up the order, you might end up with a sandwich that doesn't taste quite right.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I kind of get what you mean about the sandwich, but I still don’t really see why multiplication has to come first. If I just do it left to right, I thought I could just add the 4 after the 2. So, how would I know when to use brackets then?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Think of it like making a pizza. First, you put the dough down (multiplication), then you add the sauce and toppings (addition), and finally, you cut slices to share (subtraction). If you change the order, you might end up with a pizza that doesn't quite match the recipe. Imagine you were doing this with everyday objects you can see and touch — would your method still give the right answer?
